contents.html: The Secure Data Network System (SDNS) architecture and a set of associated specifications were developed through a multi-organizational project sponsored by the National Security Agency (NSA). They are presented here as a basis for standardization of security services in the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) architecture. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) intends to encourage widespread adoption of the resulting standards and the implementation of these security services into a wide spectrum of vendor products.
contents.html_ja: セキュアデータネットワークシステム（SDNS）のアーキテクチャと一連の関連仕様は、国家安全保障局（NSA）が後援する複数組織によるプロジェクトを通じて開発されました。これらは、開放型システム間相互接続（OSI）アーキテクチャにおけるセキュリティサービスの標準化の基礎として、ここに示されています。国立標準技術研究所（NIST）は、その結果として生まれる標準が広く採用されること、およびこれらのセキュリティサービスが幅広いベンダー製品に実装されることを促進するつもりです。

contents.html: NIST is publishing the specifications that resulted from Phase I of the SDNS project for review and comment from potential government and commercial users of security products. The specifications are not complete or totally consistent, either internally or with a number of other security projects in the National and International Standards arena. Readers of these documents should recognize that these specifications are subject to modification for various reasons as they progress through the standards process. The sponsor and participants in the SDNS project are acknowledged for the work accomplished and their support in developing and releasing these specifications.
contents.html_ja: NIST は、SDNS プロジェクトのフェーズ I の成果である仕様を、セキュリティ製品の潜在的な政府ユーザーおよび民間ユーザーによるレビューと意見を求めて公表します。これらの仕様は、内部的にも、国内および国際標準の分野にある他の多くのセキュリティプロジェクトとの間でも、完全でも完全に整合してもいません。これらの文書の読者は、これらの仕様が、標準化の過程を進むにつれて、さまざまな理由で変更される可能性があることを認識すべきです。SDNS プロジェクトの後援者および参加者に、達成された作業と、これらの仕様の開発および公開への支援について謝意を表します。

contents.html: The SDNS project was initiated by NSA to investigate methods of implementing security in a distributed computer network. The results of this project include a set of specifications that include security services, protocols and mechanisms for protecting user data in networks that are based on the OSI computer network model. Productive security services that protect user data are specified and supportive security services, such as key management and access control, are also provided. No cryptographic algorithms are included in these specifications.
contents.html_ja: SDNS プロジェクトは、分散コンピューターネットワークにセキュリティを実装する方法を調査するために NSA が開始しました。このプロジェクトの成果には、OSI コンピューターネットワークモデルに基づくネットワークでユーザーデータを保護するためのセキュリティサービス、プロトコルおよびメカニズムを含む一連の仕様が含まれます。ユーザーデータを保護する実用的なセキュリティサービスが規定されており、鍵管理やアクセス制御などの補助的なセキュリティサービスも提供されています。これらの仕様には、暗号アルゴリズムは含まれていません。

contents.html: NISTIR 90-4250 includes four security protocol documents developed by the National Security Agency (NSA) as output from the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) project. SDN.301 provides the framework for security at layer 3 (SP3) of the OSI model. The SP3 protocol provides connectionless network service with confidentiality, integrity, or both. SDN.301.1, an addendum to SDN.301, discusses an optional mechanism for providing routing flexibility in internetworks.
contents.html_ja: NISTIR 90-4250 には、セキュアデータネットワークシステム（SDNS）プロジェクトの成果として国家安全保障局（NSA）が開発した、4つのセキュリティプロトコル文書が含まれています。SDN.301 は、OSI モデルのレイヤ3におけるセキュリティ（SP3）の枠組みを提供します。SP3 プロトコルは、機密性、完全性、またはその両方を備えたコネクションレス型ネットワークサービスを提供します。SDN.301.1 は SDN.301 の補遺で、インターネットワークにおけるルーティングの柔軟性を提供する任意のメカニズムを論じています。

contents.html: Cryptographic techniques to provide data protection for transport connections or for connectionless-mode transmission are described in SDN.401. Two classes of Transport layer security (SP4) are discussed in the document. SP4C is connection oriented protection in which each transport connection is individually protected with a different cryptographic key. End system to end system protection in which all connections between a pair of end systems are protected with the same cryptographic key is provided by SP4E.
contents.html_ja: トランスポート接続またはコネクションレスモードの伝送にデータ保護を提供する暗号技術は、SDN.401 に記述されています。この文書では、トランスポート層セキュリティ（SP4）の2つのクラスを論じています。SP4C はコネクション指向の保護で、各トランスポート接続が、それぞれ異なる暗号鍵で個別に保護されます。SP4E は、エンドシステムからエンドシステムへの保護を提供し、一対のエンドシステム間のすべての接続が同じ暗号鍵で保護されます。

contents.html: Specifications for message security service and protocol are contained in SDN.701. This document describes the additions to the CCITT X.400 Message Handling System Recommendations that permit any type of message to be sent and received securely. The Message Security Protocol provides writer to reader confidentiality, integrity, data origin authentication, non-repudiation with proof of origin, access control for message transfer, and request of a signed receipt of the received message.
contents.html_ja: メッセージのセキュリティサービスとプロトコルの仕様は、SDN.701 に含まれています。この文書は、あらゆる種類のメッセージを安全に送受信できるようにする、CCITT X.400 メッセージ処理システム勧告への追加事項を記述しています。Message Security Protocol は、書き手から読み手への機密性、完全性、データ起源認証、発信元証明付きの否認防止、メッセージ転送のアクセス制御、および受信したメッセージへの署名付き受領証の要求を提供します。

contents.html: Directory System Specifications for Message Security Protocol are covered in SDN.702. This document specifies additions to the Directory System described in the 1988 X.500 series of CCITT Recommendations to support some key management functions for use by X.400 messages protected by SDNS Message Security Protocol. New attribute types and object classes for inclusion in the Directory Information Base (DIB) in support of these functions are discussed.
contents.html_ja: Message Security Protocol のディレクトリシステム仕様は、SDN.702 で扱っています。この文書は、SDNS Message Security Protocol で保護された X.400 メッセージが使う一部の鍵管理機能を支援するため、CCITT 勧告の1988年版 X.500 シリーズに記述されたディレクトリシステムへの追加事項を規定しています。これらの機能を支援するためにディレクトリ情報ベース（DIB）に含める、新しい属性型とオブジェクトクラスを論じています。

contents.html: The SDNS architecture, and its associated specifications, were developed as a cooperative project between government and industry. The project was sponsored by the National Security Agency, and supported by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (formerly the National Bureau of Standards) and the Defense Communications Agency. Twelve leading U.S. companies in computers and telecommunications made significant contributions of their technical talents and development resources. The combined efforts of these organizations produced the basis for improved security technology, interoperable security standards, and cost-effective security for computers and telecommunications.
contents.html_ja: SDNS アーキテクチャとその関連仕様は、政府と産業界の協力プロジェクトとして開発されました。このプロジェクトは国家安全保障局が後援し、国立標準技術研究所（旧米国標準局）と国防通信局（Defense Communications Agency）が支援しました。コンピューターおよび電気通信分野の米国の主要企業12社が、技術力と開発資源の面で大きく貢献しました。これらの組織の共同の取り組みにより、改善されたセキュリティ技術、相互運用可能なセキュリティ標準、およびコンピューターと電気通信の費用対効果の高いセキュリティの基礎が生まれました。

contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p16: p16 のページ番号「- 4 -」と p17 の見出し・第 1〜2 段落が 1 ブロックに入っていた。ページ番号を除き、見出しと段落に分ける。文字層に無い「8648」を画像から補う

contents.html_ja: SP3 プロトコルは、米国政府の SDNS（Secure Data Network System）活動の下で定義された複数のプロトコルの1つです。このプロトコルの目的は、暗号メカニズムの利用を通じて、さまざまなセキュリティサービスを提供することです。この文書は、プロトコルが提供するサービス、プロトコルが置く前提、プロトコルが使うプロトコルデータユニット（PDU）の書式、およびプロトコルが果たす機能を定義します。
contents.html: The SP3 Protocol is one of a number of protocols defined under the United States Government SDNS (Secure Data Network System) activity. The purpose of this protocol is to provide various security services, through the use of cryptographic mechanisms. This document defines the services provided by the protocol, the assumptions made by the protocol, the formats of the Protocol Data Units (PDUs) used by the protocol, and the functions performed by the protocol.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p16: p16 のページ番号「- 4 -」と p17 の見出し・第 1〜2 段落が 1 ブロックに入っていた。ページ番号を除き、見出しと段落に分ける。文字層に無い「8648」を画像から補う

contents.html_ja: SP3 は、ISO 8648 で定義された SNICP（subnetwork independent convergence protocol。サブネットワーク独立収束プロトコル）です。SP3 プロトコルは、機密性、完全性、またはその両方を備えたコネクションレス型ネットワークサービスを提供します。SP3 の基本的な動作モードは、NSDU（ネットワークサービスデータユニット）のカプセル化です。特定の動作モードでは、SP3 はネットワーク層の N-PDU フラグメントを独立してカプセル化することもできます。
contents.html: SP3 is a SNICP (subnetwork independent convergence protocol) as defined in ISO 8648. The SP3 protocol provides connectionless network service with confidentiality, integrity, or both. The basic mode of operation of SP3 is encapsulation of NSDUs (network service data units). In certain modes of operation, SP3 can also independently encapsulate network layer N-PDU fragments.

contents.html: The service which SP3 assumes from the sublayer below it is the connectionless network service, as defined by ISO 8348/DAD1. Thus, SP3 might, as an example, interface with the ISO CLNP protocol (ISO 8473) at its lower boundary.
contents.html_ja: SP3 が下位のサブレイヤに期待するサービスは、ISO 8348/DAD1 で定義されたコネクションレス型ネットワークサービスです。したがって SP3 は、たとえば下位の境界で ISO CLNP プロトコル（ISO 8473）とインターフェースをとることができます。

contents.html_ja: SP3 エンティティは、エンドシステムに置くことも、一定の前提の下で中間システムに置くこともできます。
contents.html: An SP3 entity may be located either at an end system, or, with certain assumptions, at an intermediate system.

contents.html_ja: SP3 プロトコルは、暗号鍵とそれらの鍵に関連付けられた属性の供給を、外部の鍵サービスに大きく依存しています。鍵に関連付けられた属性には、その鍵を使って送信される可能性のあるデータのセキュリティ属性だけでなく、使用する SP3 ヘッダ書式のオプションも含まれます。
contents.html: The SP3 protocol is heavily dependent on an external key service for supply of cryptographic keys and the attributes associated with those keys. The attributes associated with a key include not only security attributes of the data which may be sent using that key, but also the SP3 header format options to be used.

contents.html: Note: The SP3 protocol is defined in ISO terms. However, a few details of the protocol are intended to support use with the USA DoD protocol suite, in particular interaction with the DoD IP protocol. Use with the DoD protocol suite is essentially identical with use with the ISO suite.

contents.html: This document specifies the SP3 security service and protocol. These exten to the connectionless network servie, described in ISO 8348/AD1, and the connectionless network protocol, described in ISO 8473. The purpose of SP3 is to provide various security services in the network layer, through the use of cryptographic mechanisms.

contents.html: The SP3 protocol is a SNICP (subnetwork independent convergence protocol). SP3 provides at its upper boundary a secure connectionless network service and assumes at its lower boundary a connectionless network service. SP3 uses, in a subnetwork independent fashion, the services at its lower boundary to provide an improved service at its upper boundary.
contents.html_ja: SP3 プロトコルは SNICP（サブネットワーク独立収束プロトコル）です。SP3 は、上位の境界で安全なコネクションレス型ネットワークサービスを提供し、下位の境界でコネクションレス型ネットワークサービスを想定します。SP3 は、サブネットワークに依存しない形で下位の境界のサービスを使い、上位の境界で改善されたサービスを提供します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p21: 画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: Note: if the sublayer below SP3 provides a connection-oriented service, the fundamental encapsulation function of SP3 could very likely be used to provide a connection-oriented communication service on its upper boundary. The means by which this might be done remain for further study.
contents.html_ja: 注: SP3 の下位のサブレイヤがコネクション型サービスを提供する場合、SP3 の基本的なカプセル化機能を、上位の境界でコネクション型の通信サービスを提供するために使える可能性が高いです。その方法は今後の検討課題です。

contents.html: SP3 supports access control. The key service external to SP3 may choose, for access control reasons, not to make a key available for communication between two SP3 entities. This decision by the key service implies an access control service at the upper interface of SP3, since SP3 will not allow communication if an appropriate key is not present. In addition, if a security label is provided for the data, then SP3 will make an access control check against this label on both transmit and receive.

contents.html: SP3-A -- the SP3 header contains the NSAP addresses of the source and destination end systems. This mode can be used at end systems and at intermediate systems. SP3-A always provides integrity of the SP3_Userdata and the addresses, whether or not requested by the user. Confidentiality of the SP3_Userdata is determined by the SP3_UNITDATA Request SP3_Quality_of_Service parameter

contents.html: SP3-I -- the SP3 header includes an ISO CLNP header, in the format specified in ISO 8473. This CLNP header includes the addresses of the source and destination end systems, as well as other communications parameters. The SP3-I mode can be used at end systems and at intermediate systems. It allows independent encapsulation of CLNP fragments. SP3-I always provides integrity of the Userdata and CLNP header whether or not requested by the user. Confidentiality of the SP3 Userdata is determined by the SP3_UNITDATA Request SP3_Quality_of_Service parameter.

contents.html: SP3-D -- the SP3 header includes a DoD IP header, in the format specified by MIL-STD-1777. contents.html_ja: 6.1 機能の概要
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p25: 画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: The SP3 entity has access to a "Traffic Encryption Key Management Information Base" (TEK MIB). Associated with each key in the TEK MIB are a number of attributes describing how the key is to be used. In response to an SP3_UNITDATA Request, the SP3 attempts to identify a key with proper attributes. If one is found, the SP3 constructs a protected data unit containing the SP3_Userdata of the Request and some protocol control information, uses the key to encrypt and/or compute an Integrity Check Value (ICV ) for the protected data, and adds some unprotected control information to form a PDU. The resulting PDU is then passed to the next lower sublayer as the BN_Userdata of a BN_UNITDATA Request. BN_Destination Address, BN_Source_Address, and BN_Quality_of_Service are passed to the next lower sublayer in the BN_UNITDATA Request.
contents.html_ja: SP3 エンティティは、"Traffic Encryption Key Management Information Base"（TEK MIB）にアクセスできます。TEK MIB の各鍵には、その鍵をどのように使うかを記述する複数の属性が関連付けられています。SP3 は、SP3_UNITDATA Request に応答して、適切な属性を持つ鍵の識別を試みます。見つかった場合、SP3 は、Request の SP3_Userdata といくつかのプロトコル制御情報を含む保護データユニットを構築し、その鍵を使って保護データを暗号化し、ICV（完全性チェック値）を計算し、またはその両方を行い、保護されない制御情報を追加して PDU を形成します。その結果の PDU は、BN_UNITDATA Request の BN_Userdata として次の下位サブレイヤに渡されます。BN_Destination Address、BN_Source_Address、BN_Quality_of_Service は、BN_UNITDATA Request で次の下位サブレイヤに渡されます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p25: 行の外にずれた「BN」等の断片をまとめ、語順の崩れ（ICV の括弧）を直す

contents.html: In response to a BN_UNITDATA Indication, an SP3 entity identifies the key from the key identifier carried in the PDU. The SP3 uses the key to decrypt and/or verify the ICV of the protected data. The SP3_Userdata portion of the PDU is extracted, and passed to the next layer above in the SP3_UNITDATA Indication. SP3_Destination Address, SP3_Source_Address, SP3_Quality_of_Service are derived from the related BN UNITDATA Indication parameters or protocol control information and are passed to the next layer above in the SP3_UNITDATA Indication.
contents.html_ja: SP3 エンティティは、BN_UNITDATA Indication に応答して、PDU に含まれる鍵識別子から鍵を識別します。SP3 は、その鍵を使って保護データを復号し、ICV を検証し、またはその両方を行います。PDU の SP3_Userdata 部分が取り出され、SP3_UNITDATA Indication で次の上位層に渡されます。SP3_Destination Address、SP3_Source_Address、SP3_Quality_of_Service は、関連する BN UNITDATA Indication のパラメーターまたはプロトコル制御情報から導出され、SP3_UNITDATA Indication で次の上位層に渡されます。

contents.html: Any PDU contains an integral number of octets. The octets in a PDU are numbered starting from one (1) and increasing in the order in which they are put into the Userdata parameter of a BN_UNITDATA Request. The bits in an octet are numbered from one (1) to eight (8), where bit one (1) is the low-order bit.

contents.html: Parameters which are associated with each separate PDU can be carried through a network by a connectionless network protocol. contents.html: The SDNS architecture, and its associated specifications, were developed as a cooperative project between government and industry. The project was sponsored by the National Security Agency, and supported by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (formerly the National Bureau of Standards) and the Defense Communications Agency. Twelve leading U.S. companies in computers and telecommunications made significant contributions of their technical talents and development resources. The combined efforts of these organizations produced the basis for improved security technology, interoperable security standards, and cost-effective security for computers and telecommunications.
contents.html_ja: SDNS アーキテクチャとその関連仕様は、政府と産業界の協力プロジェクトとして開発されました。このプロジェクトは国家安全保障局が後援し、国立標準技術研究所（旧米国標準局）と国防通信局（Defense Communications Agency）が支援しました。コンピューターおよび電気通信分野の米国の主要企業12社が、技術力と開発資源の面で大きく貢献しました。これらの組織の共同の取り組みにより、改善されたセキュリティ技術、相互運用可能なセキュリティ標準、ならびにコンピューターと電気通信のための費用対効果の高いセキュリティの基礎が生まれました。

contents.html: Each SE TPDU must contain the direction indicator bit (FLAGS field) indicating the sender of the TPDU. When a SE TPDU is sent by the initiator of the cryptographic association, the direction indicator bit is set to 1. When a SE TPDU is sent by the responder of the cryptographic association, the direction indicator bit is set to 0. Upon receipt of a SE TPDU the transport entity shall validate the direction indicator bit. If a SE TPDU is received with an incorrect direction indicator the TPDU shall be discarded.
contents.html_ja: 各 SE TPDU は、TPDU の送信者を示す方向指示子ビット（FLAGS フィールド）を含まなければなりません。SE TPDU が暗号アソシエーションのイニシエータによって送信される場合、方向指示子ビットは1に設定されます。SE TPDU が暗号アソシエーションのレスポンダによって送信される場合、方向指示子ビットは0に設定されます。SE TPDU を受信したら、トランスポートエンティティは方向指示子ビットを検証しなければなりません。誤った方向指示子を持つ SE TPDU を受信した場合、その TPDU は破棄しなければなりません。

contents.html: If the connection-oriented integrity service is specified for a transport connection (kg_tc and integ_yes), each TPDU shall have a unique sequence number in a CA. Neither transport entity shall transmit a new DT or ED TPDU bearing a sequence number (either TPDU-NR or ED-TPDU-NR) which was previously used with that key. Retransmissions as part of normal error control and recovery may repeat the sequence number under the original key or use a new key.When either the DT or ED sequence number space is exhausted on a particular connection, a different cryptographic key than any previously used to protect data using that connection identifier (DST-REF) shall be used for transmitting any further data TPDUs. The key replacement procedure (6.8) shall be invoked. The new key shall exist prior to this procedure being employed. If no such key exists, the connection shall be released. Upon receipt of a DT or ED TPDU which duplicates a previously received sequence number on the current cryptographic key the transport entity shall discard the TPDU.
contents.html_ja: トランスポート接続にコネクション型の完全性サービスが指定されている（kg_tc および integ_yes）場合、各 TPDU は CA 内で一意のシーケンス番号を持たなければなりません。どちらのトランスポートエンティティも、その鍵で以前に使われたシーケンス番号（TPDU-NR または ED-TPDU-NR）を付けた新しい DT TPDU または ED TPDU を送信してはなりません。通常のエラー制御と回復の一環としての再送では、元の鍵の下でシーケンス番号を繰り返してもよく、新しい鍵を使ってもよいです。特定の接続で DT または ED のシーケンス番号空間が使い尽くされた場合、それ以降のデータ TPDU の送信には、その接続識別子（DST-REF）を使ってデータの保護に以前使われたどの鍵とも異なる暗号鍵を使わなければなりません。鍵交換手順（6.8）を呼び出さなければなりません。この手順を適用する前に、新しい鍵が存在していなければなりません。そのような鍵が存在しない場合、接続を解放しなければなりません。現在の暗号鍵で以前に受信したシーケンス番号と重複する DT TPDU または ED TPDU を受信した場合、トランスポートエンティティはその TPDU を破棄しなければなりません。

contents.html: The SDNS architecture, and its associated specifications, were developed as a cooperative project between government and industry. The project was sponsored by the National Security Agency, and supported by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (formerly the National Bureau of Standards) and the Defense Communications Agency. Twelve leading U.S. companies in computers and telecommunications made significant contributions of their technical talents and development resources. The combined efforts of these organizations produced the basis for improved security technology, interoperable security standards, and cost-effective security for computers and telecommunications.
contents.html_ja: SDNS アーキテクチャとその関連仕様は、政府と産業界の協力プロジェクトとして開発されました。このプロジェクトは国家安全保障局が後援し、国立標準技術研究所（旧米国標準局）と国防通信局（Defense Communications Agency）が支援しました。コンピューターおよび電気通信分野の米国の主要企業12社が、技術的才能と開発資源の面で大きく貢献しました。これらの組織の共同の取り組みにより、改善されたセキュリティ技術、相互運用可能なセキュリティ標準、およびコンピューターと電気通信の費用対効果の高いセキュリティの基礎が生まれました。

contents.html: The requirement for secure Electronic Mail and secure messaging has resulted in the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) architecture developed in support of a secure version of the X.400 Message Handling System. This document describes the additions to the CCITT X.400 Recommendations (either 1984 or 1988) that permit any type of message (including interpersonal messages) to be sent and received securely. ANSI has defined X.400 Message Transfer System conventions for Electronic Data Interchange (EDI). Using the ANSI conventions and the SDNS security additions, EDI messages can be exchanged securely. This protocol is known as the Message Security Protocol (MSP).
contents.html_ja: 安全な電子メールと安全なメッセージングの要件から、X.400 メッセージ処理システムの安全版を支援するために開発された、セキュアデータネットワークシステム（SDNS）アーキテクチャが生まれました。この文書は、あらゆる種類のメッセージ（個人間メッセージを含む）を安全に送受信できるようにする、CCITT X.400 勧告（1984年版または1988年版）への追加事項を記述します。ANSI は、電子データ交換（EDI）のための X.400 メッセージ転送システムの規約を定義しています。ANSI の規約と SDNS のセキュリティ追加事項を使うことで、EDI メッセージを安全に交換できます。このプロトコルは、Message Security Protocol（MSP）として知られています。

contents.html: This document specifies the Message Security services and protocol that will be implemented in SDNS MHS components. contents.html: Message Security Protocol (MSP): The SDNS protocol for X.400 message security. MSP is a content protocol, and is implemented within the originator and recipient UAs. MSP processing occurs prior to submitting a message to the MTS and after accepting delivery of a message from the MTS. MSP provides security for a content protocol (e.g. IPM, EDI), but is independent of the content protocol.

contents.html: The protocol operates by encapsulating a message content in a security heading; these together form a new content type designated ProtectedContent. This new content carries the original message content (encrypted if message confidentiality is requested), plus various security parameters required by recipients to decrypt and/or validate the message upon receipt. Also included are parameters which specify the algorithms employed to perform encryption, integrity checking, and signature generation/validation, as appropriate for each service. Optionally, selected fields from the original message can be included in the security heading for perusal by the recipient prior to decryption. This facility is initially defined only for the P2 content type, but other content types can be added as needed. (Invocation of this facility may be restricted based on a particular security doctrine.) The resulting encapsulated content is submitted to the Message Transfer System (MTS) for further processing.
contents.html_ja: このプロトコルは、メッセージ内容をセキュリティヘッディングでカプセル化することで動作します。これらが合わさって、ProtectedContent と呼ばれる新しい内容種別を形成します。この新しい内容は、元のメッセージ内容（メッセージの機密性が要求されている場合は暗号化されたもの）と、受信側が受信時にメッセージを復号するか、検証するか、またはその両方を行うために必要となるさまざまなセキュリティパラメーターを運びます。また、各サービスに適した、暗号化、完全性チェック、署名の生成・検証を行うために使うアルゴリズムを指定するパラメーターも含まれます。任意で、元のメッセージから選択したフィールドを、受信側が復号の前に確認できるよう、セキュリティヘッディングに含めることができます。この機能は、当初は P2 内容種別についてのみ定義されていますが、必要に応じて他の内容種別を追加できます。（この機能の呼び出しは、特定のセキュリティ原則に基づいて制限される場合があります。）結果として得られたカプセル化された内容は、さらなる処理のためにメッセージ転送システム（MTS）に送信されます。

contents.html: The access control function is integrated within the SDNS MSP implementation. MSP operates in conjunction with the user agent (UA) process responsible for originating and receiving messages. It is technically feasible to reflect information resulting from the access control decision process to the user associated with the UA, whether the user is a human or another process. Access control implementation details are a local matter. It should be noted that access control applies only to messages for which confidentiality, integrity, and data origin authentication services are selected.
contents.html_ja: アクセス制御機能は、SDNS MSP の実装に組み込まれています。MSP は、メッセージの発信と受信を担当するユーザーエージェント（UA）のプロセスと連携して動作します。アクセス制御の決定プロセスから得られた情報を、UA に関連付けられたユーザー（人間か別のプロセスかを問いません）に反映することは、技術的に可能です。アクセス制御の実装の詳細は、ローカルマターです。アクセス制御は、機密性、完全性、データ起源認証のサービスが選択されたメッセージにのみ適用されることに留意すべきです。

contents.html: The MHS is a store-and-forward message system where messages can be addressed to multiple recipients. MSP accommodates these characteristics in the distribution of keys for use by cipher functions, in the use of several distinct encryption and integrity algorithms, and in the structure of the MSP heading.
contents.html_ja: MHS は蓄積交換型のメッセージシステムであり、メッセージを複数の受信者に宛てることができます。MSP は、これらの特性に、暗号機能が使う鍵の配布、複数の異なる暗号化・完全性アルゴリズムの使用、および MSP ヘッディングの構造において対応します。

contents.html: The originator of a message assigns the key to be used to protect the message content. The originator obtains, (e.g., from a directory server), the certificate and the UKM for each intended recipient. In preparing a message for submission, the originator collects a key for each recipient. The originator takes the message key, sensitivity label, a one-way hash on the message content and other security control information and encrypts it under this pairwise key to form a protected token. The originator then places the protected token for each recipient in the MSP heading. During this process, the originator performs access control checks to ensure that each recipient is authorized to receive the message. Each token is tagged by the originator for identification by the proper recipient. The originator's certificate and UKM are placed in the MSP heading to provide each recipient with the necessary data to process the message.
contents.html_ja: メッセージの発信者は、メッセージ内容の保護に使う鍵を割り当てます。発信者は、意図した各受信者の証明書と UKM を（たとえばディレクトリサーバーから）取得します。メッセージを送信する準備として、発信者は各受信者の鍵を収集します。発信者は、メッセージ鍵、機微度ラベル、メッセージ内容の一方向ハッシュ、およびその他のセキュリティ制御情報を取り、このペアワイズ鍵の下で暗号化して、保護トークンを作成します。その後、発信者は各受信者の保護トークンを MSP ヘッディングに置きます。この過程で、発信者は、各受信者がメッセージを受け取る権限を持つことを確実にするため、アクセス制御チェックを行います。各トークンには、適切な受信者が識別できるよう、発信者がタグを付けます。発信者の証明書と UKM は、各受信者にメッセージを処理するために必要なデータを提供するため、MSP ヘッディングに置かれます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p82: 画像と語ごとに照合。ページをまたぐ 1 段落をまとめ、見出しと誤認された UKM を文に戻す（ori^nator→originator）

contents.html: Upon receipt of the message, each recipient selects its token from the security heading using the tag as a search key. Each recipient then collects his pairwise key and decrypts his token to provide access to the message key, one way hash, and other security control information as described above. The security label is checked to enforce access control policy, the message key is used to decrypt the message, and the one way hash is used to verify the integrity of the message.
contents.html_ja: メッセージを受信すると、各受信者は、タグを検索キーとして使い、セキュリティヘッディングから自分のトークンを選択します。その後、各受信者は自分のペアワイズ鍵を収集し、自分のトークンを復号して、メッセージ鍵、一方向ハッシュ、および上述のその他のセキュリティ制御情報にアクセスします。セキュリティラベルは、アクセス制御ポリシーを実施するためにチェックされ、メッセージ鍵はメッセージの復号に使われ、一方向ハッシュはメッセージの完全性の検証に使われます。

contents.html: 5.3 Message Processing for Signatures and Signed Receipts
contents.html_ja: 5.3 署名と署名付き受領証のためのメッセージ処理
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p83: 画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: If the originator selects the non-repudiation with proof of origin service, a SignatureBlock is included in the MSP heading. This data item includes an identifier for the signature algorithm, the originator's signatureCertificate, controlInformation, and a signatureValue. To sign a message, the originator calculates a one-way hash on the (original) message content, as above, then continues the calculation to include the SignatureInformation. This field includes an encapsulatedContentType and a contentIdentifier. The resulting hash value is signed and included as the signatureValue in the SignatureBlock.
contents.html_ja: 発信者が発信元証明付きの否認防止サービスを選択した場合、SignatureBlock が MSP ヘッディングに含まれます。このデータ項目には、署名アルゴリズムの識別子、発信者の signatureCertificate、controlInformation、および signatureValue が含まれます。メッセージに署名するために、発信者は、前述のとおり（元の）メッセージ内容に対する一方向ハッシュを計算し、その後 SignatureInformation を含めるように計算を続けます。このフィールドには、encapsulatedContentType と contentIdentifier が含まれます。結果のハッシュ値に署名され、SignatureBlock に signatureValue として含められます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p83: 画像と語ごとに照合。p84 の続きまで含む。controlinformation→controlInformation、Signatureinformation→SignatureInformation、contentidentifier→contentIdentifier

contents.html: If the originator elects to request signed receipts from any or all of the recipients, this is indicated in the receiptsIndicator field of the SignatureInformation. If all recipients are requested to return such receipts, a flag is set; if a subset of the recipients are requested to return receipts, a list of their O/RNames is included in the field. An originator might maintain a database, (e.g., indexed by contentIdentifier), indicating the recipients from whom signed receipts for a specified message (and a copy of the message plus the hash value) are expected. This data will be required in support of later receipt processing. The database is a local matter and thus outside the scope of this protocol specification.
contents.html_ja: 発信者が、一部またはすべての受信者に署名付き受領証を要求することを選択した場合、これは SignatureInformation の receiptsIndicator フィールドに示されます。すべての受信者にそのような受領証の返送が要求される場合は、フラグが設定されます。受信者の一部に受領証の返送が要求される場合は、それらの O/RName の一覧がこのフィールドに含まれます。発信者は、特定のメッセージについて、どの受信者から署名付き受領証（およびメッセージの写しとハッシュ値）が期待されるかを示すデータベースを（たとえば contentIdentifier で索引付けして）維持する場合があります。このデータは、後の受領証の処理を支援するために必要となります。このデータベースはローカルマターであり、したがってこのプロトコル仕様の範囲外です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84: 画像と語ごとに照合。大文字の I の誤読、0/R→O/R

contents.html: A recipient validates a message signature in a two-step process. First, the one-way hash on the received message content and the SignatureInformation is calculated. Then he performs calculations to verify the supplied signatureValue using the information contained in the signatureCertificate.
contents.html_ja: 受信者は、2段階の過程でメッセージ署名を検証します。まず、受信したメッセージ内容と SignatureInformation に対する一方向ハッシュを計算します。次に、signatureCertificate に含まれる情報を使って、提供された signatureValue を検証するための計算を行います。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84: 画像と語ごとに照合。見出しと誤認された「A」を文に戻す

contents.html: If the recipient has been requested to return a signed receipt, as noted above, he may generate a receipt or not. To return a receipt, the recipient constructs a new SignatureBlock. This block will contain the recipient's signatureCertificate. The receiptInformation field of the ControlInformation identifies the block as a signed receipt (versus a signed message). The original hash value is extended to include the ControlInformation for the receipt and is signed by the recipient. A message consisting solely of an MSP heading containing a version number and SignatureBlock is transmitted to the originator of the signed message.
contents.html_ja: 前述のとおり、受信者が署名付き受領証の返送を要求されている場合、受信者は受領証を生成してもよいですし、しなくてもよいです。受領証を返送するには、受信者は新しい SignatureBlock を構築します。このブロックには、受信者の signatureCertificate が含まれます。ControlInformation の receiptInformation フィールドは、そのブロックが（署名付きメッセージではなく）署名付き受領証であることを識別します。元のハッシュ値は、受領証の ControlInformation を含むように拡張され、受信者によって署名されます。バージョン番号と SignatureBlock を含む MSP ヘッディングのみから成るメッセージが、署名付きメッセージの発信者に送信されます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84: 画像と語ごとに照合。見出しと誤認された「A」を文の位置に戻し、大文字の I の誤読を直す

contents.html: The originator of a message requesting signed receipts will process the receipt message using the stored message hash from the original message. This value is extended to include the ControlInformation of the receipt. The computed value is compared to the verified signature value of the receipt message. If the values match, the returned SignatureBlock serves as a signed receipt for the original message.
contents.html_ja: 署名付き受領証を要求したメッセージの発信者は、元のメッセージから保存しておいたメッセージハッシュを使って、受領証メッセージを処理します。この値は、受領証の ControlInformation を含むように拡張されます。計算された値は、受領証メッセージの検証済みの署名値と比較されます。値が一致すれば、返送された SignatureBlock は、元のメッセージの署名付き受領証として機能します。

contents.html: Data origin authentication provides corroboration to the application process that the source of the message is the claimed originator. The key used to encrypt the message content is separately encrypted for each recipient using a token key. Successful decryption of the message key and successful verification of the one-way hash provides data origin authentication.
contents.html_ja: データ起源認証は、メッセージの送信元が主張された発信者であることを、アプリケーションプロセスに対して裏付けます。メッセージ内容の暗号化に使う鍵は、トークン鍵を使って受信者ごとに別々に暗号化されます。メッセージ鍵の復号の成功と一方向ハッシュの検証の成功によって、データ起源認証が提供されます。

contents.html: Access control for message transfer is a service to both originator and recipient. The originator is prohibited from submitting, and the recipient is prohibited from receiving messages that violate the security policy.
contents.html_ja: メッセージ転送のアクセス制御は、発信者と受信者の両方に対するサービスです。発信者は、セキュリティポリシーに違反するメッセージを送信することを禁止され、受信者は、そのようなメッセージを受信することを禁止されます。

contents.html: Non-repudiation with proof of origin is a service to originator and recipient. The originator is assured that the signed message did not admit tampering. The recipient of a signed message is assured that the message sent cannot be denied. A digital signature placed in the security heading of the message binds the identity of the originator to the message content. The recipient of the message can subsequently prove to a third party that only the originator could have produced the signature.
contents.html_ja: 発信元証明付きの否認防止は、発信者と受信者に対するサービスです。発信者は、署名されたメッセージが改ざんされていないことを保証されます。署名されたメッセージの受信者は、送信されたメッセージが否認されないことを保証されます。メッセージのセキュリティヘッディングに置かれたデジタル署名は、発信者の識別情報をメッセージ内容に結び付けます。メッセージの受信者は、その後、発信者だけがその署名を作成できたことを第三者に証明できます。

contents.html: Request For Signed Receipt of the received message asks the recipient to digitally sign a hash of the message and return the signature. If the recipient performs this action and the verified receipt hash value supplied by the recipient matches that computed by the originator using the signature verification process, then the originator is provided a form of non-repudiation with proof-of-delivery service.
contents.html_ja: 受信したメッセージへの署名付き受領証の要求は、受信者に、メッセージのハッシュにデジタル署名して、その署名を返送するよう求めます。受信者がこの動作を行い、受信者が提供した検証済みの受領証ハッシュ値が、署名検証プロセスを使って発信者が計算した値と一致する場合、発信者には、配送証明付きの否認防止サービスの一形態が提供されます。

contents.html: The Request For Signed Receipt may be used only in conjunction with the non-repudiation with proof-of-origin service. The originator of a message selects which recipients are to return a signed receipt. This list is contained within the signature block in the MSP security heading. The originator's MSP process must include the list of recipients requested to return a signed receipt in the calculation of the hash used to produce the digital signature for the non-repudiation with proof of origin service.
contents.html_ja: 署名付き受領証の要求は、発信元証明付きの否認防止サービスと組み合わせる場合にのみ使用できます。メッセージの発信者は、どの受信者に署名付き受領証を返送させるかを選択します。この一覧は、MSP セキュリティヘッディングの署名ブロックに含まれます。発信者の MSP プロセスは、発信元証明付きの否認防止サービスのためのデジタル署名の作成に使うハッシュの計算に、署名付き受領証の返送を要求された受信者の一覧を含めなければなりません。

contents.html: In order to support key distribution for SDNS message security, the Directory Information Base (DIB) must store for each MSP user: certificate, a signature certificate, a set of UKMs with associated tags, and any auxiliary vectors associated with the user. The certificate, signature certificate, and any auxiliary vector(s) contain the O/R name of the user and additional identifying information. The UKMs are submitted by the user and employed in the keying process. The tags identify each UKM and a user-generated signature binds each UKM to its tag. The originator of a message accesses the directory service to obtain address information, the certificate, auxiliary vector, and tagged UKM for each recipient. {Details of these and other key management support functions provided by the directory service are contained in SDN.702 SDNS Directory Specifications for Utilization with the SDNS Message Security Protocol.}
contents.html_ja: SDNS メッセージセキュリティの鍵配布を支援するために、ディレクトリ情報ベース（DIB）は、MSP ユーザーごとに、証明書、署名証明書、関連するタグを持つ UKM の集合、およびそのユーザーに関連付けられた任意の補助ベクトルを保存しなければなりません。証明書、署名証明書、および任意の補助ベクトルには、ユーザーの O/R 名と追加の識別情報が含まれます。UKM はユーザーによって送信され、鍵処理で使われます。タグは各 UKM を識別し、ユーザーが生成した署名が各 UKM をそのタグに結び付けます。メッセージの発信者は、ディレクトリサービスにアクセスして、各受信者のアドレス情報、証明書、補助ベクトル、およびタグ付き UKM を取得します。{ディレクトリサービスが提供するこれらおよびその他の鍵管理支援機能の詳細は、SDN.702 SDNS Directory Specifications for Utilization with the SDNS Message Security Protocol に含まれています。}

contents.html: If an MSP implementation permits the use of blind carbon copies (bcc) and conf-integ-doa-ac is selected, then the MSP process must generate separate copies of the ProtectedContent to input to the SUBMIT operation. One copy should contain the protected tokens for all recipients not on the bcc list and should include these recipients in the SUBMIT argument list. If the identity of each bcc recipient is to be concealed from each other recipient (including other bcc recipients), then a SUBMIT operation should be invoked for each bcc recipient and the protected content should contain a protected token for only the designated recipient. This restriction is not needed if the message is only signed.
contents.html_ja: MSP の実装がブラインドカーボンコピー（bcc）の使用を許可していて、conf-integ-doa-ac が選択されている場合、MSP プロセスは、SUBMIT 操作に入力するために、ProtectedContent の別個のコピーを生成しなければなりません。1つのコピーには、bcc リストにない全受信者の保護トークンを含めるべきです。また、これらの受信者を SUBMIT の引数リストに含めるべきです。各 bcc 受信者の識別情報を、他のすべての受信者（他の bcc 受信者を含む）から隠す場合は、bcc 受信者ごとに SUBMIT 操作を呼び出すべきです。また、保護された内容には、指定された受信者のみの保護トークンを含めるべきです。メッセージが署名だけされている場合は、この制限は必要ありません。

contents.html: The requestForSignedReceipt flag indicates that the originator has requested one or more recipients to return a signed copy of the received message. The contentIdentifier is an octet string used to uniquely identify the message among all those submitted by the originator. The ReceiptsIndicator is either an integer with value 1, indicating that ALL recipients should be requested to return a signed receipt, a sequence of O/R names identifying the recipients who are to be explicitly requested to respond with a signed receipt, or an integer with value 0, indicating that no receipts are requested. As above, in order to provide maximum privacy in the context of blind carbon copies, multiple submissions will be required to prevent a ReceiptsIndicator sequence from disclosing identities of bcc recipients.

contents.html: The ProtectedToken comprises the msgKey, msgHash, Sensitivity, encapsulatedContentType, signatureBlockIndicator and token-integrity-check. The msgKey is the key used by the encryption function identified by the confidentialityAlgorithm to encrypt the message body. The msgHash is the result of the checkfunction applied to the entire Content. The checkfunction is identified by the integrityAlgorithm. The Sensitivity indicates the security level of the encrypted portions of the message. The encapsulatedContentType identifies the type of the original content before MSP processing. The signatureBlockIndicator is a flag indicating to the recipient that the originator has requested a signature block. The token-integrity-check is the result of an integrity function applied to the concatenation of the msgKey, msgHash, sensitivity, encapsulatedContentType, and signatureBlockIndicator. contents.html: If, as described in section 8.2.2.7, a signed receipt is requested by the originator and the recipient elects to comply with the request, a SignatureBlock is constructed. The SignatureBlock contains SignatureCertificate of this recipient and the SignatureInformation specifies a signed receipt as the signatureType. That is, signatureType is set to signedReceipt (2). The signatureValue is computed by signing the signatureValue of the original message and the ControlInformation in the receipt. The resulting SignatureBlock is concatenated with the version to form an MSP message and is submitted to the originator of the received, signed message.

contents.html: This document specifies additions to the Directory System described in the 1988 X.500 series of CCITT Recommendations to support some key management functions, both for general use by SDNS components and, in particular, for use by X.400 messages protected by SDNS Message Security Protocol (MSP). This document describes the new attribute types and object classes for inclusion in the Directory Information Base (DIB) in support of these functions. These new attributes will be manipulated using the Directory Access Protocol (DAP), but no new operations are required to manipulate these attributes. None of these attributes are interpreted by the Directory, and none are used for naming.
contents.html_ja: この文書は、SDNS コンポーネントによる一般的な使用と、特に SDNS Message Security Protocol（MSP）で保護された X.400 メッセージによる使用のために、一部の鍵管理機能を支援するための、CCITT 勧告の1988年版 X.500 シリーズに記述されたディレクトリシステムへの追加事項を規定します。この文書は、これらの機能を支援するためにディレクトリ情報ベース（DIB）に含める、新しい属性型とオブジェクトクラスを記述します。これらの新しい属性は、ディレクトリアクセスプロトコル（DAP）を使って操作されますが、これらの属性を操作するために新しい操作は必要ありません。これらの属性は、いずれもディレクトリによって解釈されず、いずれも命名には使われません。

contents.html: These attributes consist of values, each of which is a SignedUkm. The signature can be validated using the signature certificate stored with the Directory entry. contents.html: These additions to the DIB do not require any new services, but rather, specify new attributes which may be parameters to existing services as defined in X.511. Using these services, a DUA can retrieve the values of these attributes, modify the attribute values, and set the entry access control (A.C.) parameters associated with these attributes, subject to the A.C. restrictions. It is suggested that the default A.C. parameters of each of these new attributes be set to permit readItem access for all accessors, and modifyItem access for the owner(s) of each entry. The Secure Data Network System (SDNS) architecture and a set of associated specifications were developed through a multi-organizational project sponsored by the National Security Agency (NSA) They are presented here as a basis for standardization of

security services in the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) architecture. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) intends to encourage widespread adoption of the resulting standards and the implementation of these security services into a wide spectrum of vendor products.

NIST is publishing the specifications that resulted from Phase I of the SDNS project for review and comment from potential government and commercial users of security products. The specifications are not complete or totally consistent, either internally or with a number of other security projects in the National and International Standards arena. Readers of these documents should recognize that these specifications are subject to modification for various reasons as they progress through the standards process. The sponsor and participants in the SDNS project are acknowledged for the work accomplished and their support in developing and releasing these specifications.

The SDNS project was initiated by NSA to investigate methods of implementing security in a distributed computer network. The results of this project include a set of specifications that include security services, protocols and mechanisms for protecting user data in networks that are based on the OSI computer network model. Productive security services that protect user data are specified and supportive security services, such as key management and access control, are also provided. No cryptographic algorithms are included in these specifications.

NIST is working with NSA and industry to identify and develop a framework of base standards for network security. In 1989, NIST established the OSI Security Laboratory where interested researchers from government and industry develop and demonstrate new ideas in network security. The major goals of NIST's network security activities are to:
Identify and develop ’security standards for open systems
Specify a key management system that supports these
Encourage the development of interoperable equipment
Requirements for Support of the SDNS Key Management Protocol Message Security Protocol
SDNS Directory Specifications for Utilization with
the SDNS Message Security Protocol Access Control Concepts Document
Key Management Protocol - Definition of Services
Provided by the Key Management Application Service Element Key Management Protocol - Specification of the
Protocol for Services Provided by the Key Management Application Service Element Key Management Protocol - SDNS Traffic Key Attribute

Because of the wide spread interest in the SDNS project, NIST is publishing these ten documents as three Reports entitled: Security Protocols, Key Management, and Access Control. The following diagram shows the relationship and contents of these reports.

NISTIR 90-4250 includes four security protocol documents developed by the National Security Agency (NSA) as output from the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) project. SDN. 301 provides the framework for security at layer 3 (SP3) of the OSI model. The SP3 protocol provides connectionless network service with confidentiality, integrity, or both. SDN. 301.1, an addendum to SDN. 301, discusses an optional mechanism for providing routing flexibility in internetworks

Cryptographic techniques to provide data protection for transport connections or for connectionless-mode transmission are described in SDN. 401. Two classes of Transport layer security (SP4) are discussed in the document. SP4C is connection oriented protection in which each transport connection is individually protected with a different cryptographic key. End system to end system protection in which all connections between a pair of end systems are protected with the same cryptographic key is provided by SP4E.

Specifications for message security service and protocol are contained in SDN. 701. This document describes the additions to the CCITT X.400 Message Handling System Recommendations that permit any type of message to be sent and received securely. The Message Security Protocol provides writer to reader confidentiality, integrity, data origin authentication, non-repudiation with proof of origin, access control for message transfer, and request of a signed receipt of the received message.

Directory System Specifications for Message Security Protocol are covered in SDN. 702. This document specifies additions to the Directory System described in the 1988 X.500 series of CCITT Recommendations to support some key management functions for use by X.400 messages protected by SDNS Message Security Protocol. New attribute types and object classes for inclusion in the Directory Information Base (DIB) in support of these functions are discussed.

The security protocols addressed in NISTIR 90-4250 are heavily dependent on a cryptographic management and access control service. The SDNS specifications for these services are contained in NISTIR 90-4262 and NISTIR 90-4259, respectively.

_ 4 -0 Introduction The SP3 Protocol is one of a number of protocols defined under the United States Government SDNS (Secure Data Network System) activity. The purpose of this protocol is to provide various security services, through the use of cryptographic mechanisms. This document defines the services provided by the protocol, the assumptions made by the protocol, the formats of the Protocol Data Units (PDUs) used by the protocol, and the functions performed by the protocol. SP3 is a SNICP (subnetwork independent convergence protocol) as defined in ISO
The SP3 protocol provides connectionless network service with confidentiality,

integrity, or both. The basic mode of operation of SP3 is encapsulation of NSDUs (network service data units). In certain modes of operation, SP3 can also independently encapsulate network layer N-PDU fragments. The service which SP3 assumes from the sublayer below it is the connectionless network service, as defined by ISO 8348/DAD 1. Thus, SP3 might, as an example, interface with the ISO CLNP protocol (ISO 8473) at its lower boundary. An SP3 entity may be located either at an end system, or, with certain assumptions, at an intermediate system. The SP3 protocol is heavily dependent on an external key service for supply of cryptographic keys and the attributes associated with those keys. The attributes associated with a key include not only security attributes of the data which may be sent using that key, but also the SP3 header format options to be used. The SP3 protocol is a SNICP (subnetwork independent convergence protocol). SP3 provides at its upper boundary a secure connectionless network service and assumes at its lower boundary a connectionless network service. SP3 uses, in a subnetwork independent fashion, the services at its lower boundary to provide an improved service at its upper boundary.

Note: if the sublayer below SP3 provides a connection-oriented service, the fundamental encapsulation function of SP3 could very likely be used to provide a connection-oriented communication service on its upper boundary. The means by which this might be done remain for further study.

Some other method (such as physical protection of the subnetwork) must be used to provide security between B and C if required.

Note that the SNICP in end system C does not have a peer in system A; instead its peer is at intermediate system B. Thus the protocol conducted by the SNICP at C ends at B. Minimum essential requirements are capabilities which must be present in each SP3 implementation. The options used by SP3 are negotiated for each key, and are fixed for each key.

The addressing mode is a negotiated option. Every SP3 running at an end system must implement SP3-N and SP3-A. Other addressing modes are optional. Every SP3 running at an intermediate system must implement SP3-A. SP3-N is not suitable for use by intermediate systems. SP3-I and SP3-D are optional.
Every SP3 implementation must be capable of providing both integrity and confidentiality. Integrity-only and confidentiality-only are optional services.
Type I SP3 implementations must be capable of providing the security-label service. Labels are optional for Type EE.
The use of padding is not negotiable. Every SP3 implementation must be capable of receiving and stripping the PAD option. Generation of padding is an optional capability.

This section describes the operation of SP3 using various addressing modes. SP3 is defined to provide a connectionless network service. Its request and indication parameters are consistent with that definition.
9.1 SP3 Operation at an End System

This section describes SP3 operation at an end system, using different addressing modes. The transmission functions are as described in Section 6.4, and the reception functions are as described in Section 6.5. SP3 is defined to provide a connectionless network service. Its request and indication parameters are consistent with that definition. At end systems, a transmitting SP3 always operates on NSDUs, and a receiving SP3 delivers NSDUs to the layer above it.

This mode is identical to SP4E. It is used only from end-system to end-system. SP3N encapsulates complete NSDUs. It does not include any addressing information in the encapsulated header. Network address information passed to SP3N by the transport layer is used in selecting the appropriate key and are then passed to the underlying network communications protocol in the SP3 service request. Network address information passed to SP3N in the network indication are validated against the key-ID and are passed to the transport layer in the SP3 indication.

SP3A also encapsulates complete NSDUs. The addressing information included in the encapsulated header is that passed to the source SP3 in the service request, namely source and destination end-system NSAP addresses. The source address passed in the SP3 service is the NSAP address associated with the source SP3. The

In the absence of SP3, the unit would be routed through one of the intermediate systems Dl ... Dn. If one of the Ds is unavailable, traffic will be re-routed through another in a transparent fashion.

With SP3, in the absence of the special cooperating family capabilities, E will encrypt the unit in some key which is held by some particular D, say D2. The encrypted unit must be sent to D2, since it cannot be processed by any other of the Ds.

However, there is a second difficulty: Due to the nature of cryptographic algorithms, what is encrypted as one unit must be decrypted as one unit; fragments cannot be decrypted. So, suppose D1 ... Therefore, in the absence of a special capability on the part of the Ds to handle this situation, the encryptor E must somehow arrange that all fragments of an encrypted unit arrive at the same decryptor.

The "reassemble fragments" capability on the part of the Ds means that the Ds are able to gather fragments of an encrypted unit arriving at multiple Ds together at a single one of the Ds and reassemble and process them.

The transport protocol specified in International Standard (ISO) 8073 provides the connection oriented transport service described in ISO 8072. The transport protocol specified in ISO 8602 provides the connectionless-mode transport service described in ISO 8072/DADl. ISO 8072 describes Transport Connection (TC) protection as the prevention of unauthorized monitoring or manipulation of Transport Service (TS) user data. The TS users specify TC protection qualitatively by selecting one of four TC protection quality of service options during the TC establishment phase:
a) no protection features; b) protection against passive monitoring; c) protection against modification, replay, addition or deletion; d) both b and c.
DP 7498/2 on OSI Security Architecture uses the following terms for these security services:

a) no security services; b) connection/connectionless confidentiality; c) connection/connectionless integrity (with or without recovery); and d) both connection/connectionless confidentiality and integrity.
The two subclasses of SP4 are distinguished on the basis of the granularity of cryptographic associations that are established. They are:
SP4C: Connection oriented protection in which each transport connection is
individually protected with a different cryptographic key; can provide full connection integrity and confidentiality.
SP4E: End system to end system protection in which all connections between a
pair of end systems are protected with the same cryptographic key; can provide connectionless integrity and confidentiality.

The protocol specified in this addendum to the ISO 8073 requires the availability of cryptographic keys prior to an instance of protected communication. Keys are established by a combination of system, layer and security management functions. Any specific procedure for establishing keys is outside the scope of this document. The specific procedures for maintaining cryptographic key storage as well as for associating keys with specific TPDUs, are considered a local matter.
Both the sending and receiving transport entities must use the same cryptographic algorithm or algorithms. The assumptions regarding cryptographic algorithms are as follows:
1) The same algorithm may be used for providing both confidentiality and integrity services.
2) It is beyond the scope of this document to specify a particular algorithm or to assess the security strengths or weaknesses of particular algorithms.
3) Encipherment and decipherment is performed in multiples of octets.

Encapsulation is used in conjunction with the encipherment and/or cryptographic check function to provide the connection or connectionless confidentiality and integrity services. When used by the sending entity, encapsulation is applied subsequent to all other protocol processing functions as described in ISO 8073 and ISO 8602. Further concatenation (in accordance with the concatenation rules described in 6.1) may occur after encapsulation. Decapsulation is applied by the receiving entity prior to any other protocol processing functions.

An encipherment mechanism provides data confidentiality. Each SE TPDU contains sufficient information for decipherment independent of information in any other SE TPDU. This includes identification of the cryptographic key (KEY-ID) to be used for decipherment as well as any cryptographic synchronization or algorithm initialization sequences.
An integrity function provides data and/or data stream integrity. The elements of integrity and the mechanisms used to provide them are:
Modification protection is provided by a ICV computed over the protected header and encapsulated TPDU.
Insertion protection is provided by the use of the ICV and the transport sequence numbers.
Deletion protection is provided by the use of the ICV and the transport sequence numbers.
Connection truncation protection is provided by the transmission of final sequence numbers during connection release (fsnjes).
Connection replay protection is provided by the use of a separate key per transport connection (kg tc).
Protection against replay of a is provided by the use of a separate key per transport connection (kg tc) and the use of unique sequence numbers under each key.
Reflection protection is provided by the use of a direction indicator (FLAGS field) in each SE TPDU (see 8.2. 2. 2).

The requirement for secure Electronic Mail and secure messaging has resulted in the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) architecture developed in support of a secure version of the X.400 Message Handling System. This document describes the additions to the CCITT X.400 Recommendations (either 1984 or 1988) that permit any type of message (including interpersonal messages) to be sent and received securely. ANSI has defined X.400 Message Transfer System conventions for Electronic Data Interchange (EDI). Using the ANSI conventions and the SDNS security additions, EDI messages can be exchanged securely. This protocol is known as the Message Security Protocol (MSP).

This document specifies the Message Security services and protocol that will be implemented in SDNS MHS components. The User Agent provides these services by encapsulating the message content and adding a Message Security Protocol heading before submission to the Message Transfer System. SDNS MSP is transparent to the X.400 MTS.

The Message Security Protocol provides writer to reader confidentiality, integrity, data origin authentication, non-repudiation with proof of origin, access control for message transfer, and request for a signed receipt of the received message.

For the purposes of this document the following definitions apply:
Directory service (DS): directory server containing information (e.g., certificates, auxiliary vectors, and user keying material) corresponding to recipient UAs.

Message Security Protocol (MSP): The SDNS protocol for X.400 message security. MSP is a content protocol, and is implemented within the originator and recipient UAs. MSP processing occurs prior to submitting a message to the MTS and after accepting delivery of a message from the MTS. MSP provides security for a content protocol (e.g. IPM, EDI), but is independent of the content protocol.
Originator UA: The user agent process which originates a message.
Recipient UA: The user agent process which receives a message.

The Message Security Protocol (MSP) operates on messages of any type, including, but not restricted to, Interpersonal Messages (EPMs) as defined in X.420. Thus, the term "message” is used throughout this document to refer to any content type defined for transfer by the Message Handling System, reflecting the wide applicability of this protocol. The set of security services provided by this protocol are grouped as indicated below:
message confidentiality, integrity, data origin authentication and access control
message non-repudiation with proof of origin
request for a signed receipt of the received message (only available if non-repudiation with proof of origin is selected)

The protocol operates by encapsulating a message content in a security heading; these together form a new content type designated ProtectedContent. This new content carries the original message content (encrypted if message confidentiality is requested), plus various security parameters required by recipients to decrypt and'or validate the message upon receipt. Also included are parameters which specify the algorithms employed to perform encryption, integrity checking, and signature generation/validation, as appropriate for each service. Optionally, selected fields from the original message can be included in the security heading for perusal by the recipient prior to decryption. This facility is initially defined only for the P2 content type, but other content types can be added as needed. (Invocation of this facility may be restricted based on a particular security doctrine.) The resulting encapsulated content is submitted to the Message Transfer System (MTS) for further processing.

The access control function is integrated within the SDNS MSP implementation. MSP operates in conjunction with the user agent (UA) process responsible for originating and receiving messages. It is technically feasible to reflect information resulting from the access control decision process to the user associated with the UA, whether the user is a human or another process. Access control implementation details are a local matter. It should be noted that access control applies only to messages for which confidentiality, integrity, and data origin authentication services are selected.

The is a store-and-forward message system where messages can be addressed to multiple recipients. MSP accommodates these characteristics in the distribution of keys for use by cipher functions, in the use of several distinct encryption and
integrity algorithms, and in the structure of the heading.
The originator of a message assigns the key to be used to protect the message content.

The originator obtains, (e.g., from a directory server), the certificate and the for each intended recipient. In preparing a message for submission, the originator collects a key for each recipient. The originator takes the message key, sensitivity label, a one-way hash on the message content and other security control information and encrypts it under this pairwise key to form a protected token. The originator then places the protected token for each recipient in the MSP heading. During this process, the originator performs access control checks to ensure that each recipient is authorized to receive the message. Each token is tagged by the originator for
identification by the proper recipient. The ori^nator’s certificate and are placed in the MSP heading to provide each recipient with the necessary data to process the message.

Upon receipt of the message, each recipient selects its token from the security heading using the tag as a search key. Each recipient then collects his pairwise key and decrypts his token to provide access to the message key, one way hash, and other security control information as described above. The security label is checked to enforce access control policy, the message key is used to decrypt the message, and the one way hash is used to verify the integrity of the message.

Connectionless confidentiality protects data from unauthorized disclosure. This service is provided by an encryption mechanism that is applied to the message content.
Connectionless integrity protects data from modification. This service is provided by a one-way hash applied to the plaintext message content.

Data origin authentication provides corroboration to the application process that the source of the message is the claimed originator. The key used to encrypt the message content is separately encrypted for each recipient using a token key. Successful decryption of the message key and successful verification of the one-way hash provides data origin authentication.

Access control for message transfer is a service to both originator and recipient. The originator is prohibited from submitting, and the recipient is prohibited from receiving messages that violate the security policy.

Non-repudiation with proof of origin is a service to originator and recipient. The originator is assured that the signed message did not admit tampering. The recipient of a signed message is assured that the message sent cannot be denied. A digital signature placed in the security heading of the message binds the identity of the originator to the message content. The recipient of the message can subsequently prove to a third party that only the originator could have produced the signature.

Request For Signed Receipt of the received message asks the recipient to digitally sign a hash of the message and return the signature. If the recipient performs this action and the verified receipt hash value supplied by the recipient matches that computed by the originator using the signature verification process, then the originator is provided a form of non-repudiation with proof-of-delivery service.

The Request For Signed Receipt may be used only in conjunction with the non-repudiation with proof-of-origin service. The originator of a message selects which recipients are to return a signed receipt. This list is contained within the signature block in the MSP security heading. The originator’s MSP process must include the list of recipients requested to return a signed receipt in the calculation of the hash used to produce the digital signature for the non-repudiation with proof of origin service.

This document provides the framework for the SDNS Directory Server Specification. This document is being circulated for comment and approval. It is subject to change during the development phase of SDNS.

This document specifies additions to the Directory System described in the 1988 X.500 series of CCITT Recommendations to support some key management functions, both for general use by SDNS components and, in particular, for use by X.400 messages protected by SDNS Message Security Protocol (MSP). This document describes the new attribute types and object classes for inclusion in the Directory Information Base (DIB) in support of these functions. These new attributes will be manipulated using the Directory Access Protocol (DAP), but no new operations are required to manipulate these attributes. None of these attributes are interpreted by the Directory, and none are used for naming.

In order to support key distribution for X.400 messages protected by MSP, the DIB must store some attributes, which are not currently provided as Directory attributes, in Directory entries associated with mail system users

It is anticipated that, in normal operation, a Directory User Agent (DUA) would query a Directory System Agent (DSA), using the DAP to retrieve attributes associated with one or more entries, based on asserted attribute values that are sufficient to identify the intended recipient(s).
It is assumed that both private and administrative Directories may be employed in support of SDNS electronic messages and that both Type I and Type II users will be supported.

original_blocks.html: SP3I encapsulates complete NSDUs or fragments. The transmitting SP3I constructs a CLNP header for the entire NSDU. This header includes the source and destination NSAP addresses from the service request and other QOS parameters. If fragmentation is necessary before encapsulation, this is done. The fragments (or complete data unit) are them encapsulated and passed to the lower layer for transmission. The source address passed in the SP3 service request is the NSAP address associated with the source SP3. The destination address passed with the service request is the NSAP address associated with the destination SP3.
